scope: Optional authenticated local result transport for existing GUI-owned MCP operations; not complete M2 acceptance
behavior: Pairing and command polling remain HTTP. When both sides advertise support, large replies use one session-bound loopback WebSocket; absent or pre-send unavailable channels fall back to HTTP. A failure after sending disconnects instead of replaying an ambiguous result. Public MCP tools, schemas, structured results, artifact limits, request receipts and shared application operations remain unchanged.
securityAndLifecycle: Host, Origin, token and browser session are checked; the socket is bound to the original session, only a delivered request can be resolved once, and browser acknowledgments must match its request ID. Four sockets and a five-second unauthenticated lease bound handshakes; messages are limited to 2 MiB and binary frames are rejected. Session disconnect, expiry and bridge shutdown close owned sockets. The package lock pins ws 8.22.1. These focused checks are not a claim of an exhaustive security audit.
